note: Original IELTS Speaking Part 2 style cue cards written for Bo-ok, each with a category and Part 3 discussion questions.

cards.title: Describe a book you read that you found useful.
cards.explain: and explain why you found it useful.
followUp: Do people read less than they used to?
Should schools choose the books students read?
Will printed books disappear?
What kinds of books are popular with young people in your country?
Is it better to read a book or watch the film made from it?

cards.title: Describe a skill you learned as an adult.
cards.explain: and explain how you feel about it now.
followUp: Is it harder to learn new things as we get older?
Should employers pay for workers to learn new skills?
Which skills will be most important in the future?
Which skills will be most useful in the future?
Is it easier for children or adults to learn new skills? Why?

cards.title: Describe a quiet place you like to go to.
cards.explain: and explain why you like it.
followUp: Why do some people prefer noisy places?
Are cities becoming too noisy?
How can city planners create more quiet spaces?
Why do some people find cities stressful?
Should governments create more quiet public spaces?

cards.title: Describe a person who gave you good advice.
cards.explain: and explain how it helped you.
followUp: Do young people listen to advice from older people?
Is advice from friends better than advice from experts?
Has the internet changed where people get advice?
Do young people today listen to advice from older people?
Is advice from friends more useful than advice from experts?

cards.title: Describe a journey that took longer than you expected.
cards.explain: and explain how you felt about it.
followUp: How has travel changed in your country?
Should governments invest more in public transport?
Will people travel less in the future?
How has travel changed in the last fifty years?
Should people be encouraged to use public transport? How?

cards.title: Describe an important decision you made.
cards.explain: and explain why it was important.
followUp: Do people make better decisions alone or in groups?
Why do some people find decisions difficult?
Should children be allowed to make important decisions?
Do people today have too many choices?
Should parents make important decisions for their teenage children?

cards.title: Describe a piece of technology you use every day.
points: how long you have had it
cards.explain: and explain how your life would be different without it.
followUp: Do people depend too much on technology?
How has technology changed the way people work?
Should there be limits on children's screen time?
Has technology made people more or less sociable?
What are the risks of depending on technology?

cards.title: Describe a celebration you enjoyed.
cards.explain: and explain why you enjoyed it.
followUp: Are traditional celebrations still important?
Why do some people spend a lot of money on celebrations?
How do celebrations differ between generations?
Why are traditional celebrations important for a society?
Do people spend too much money on celebrations nowadays?

cards.title: Describe a goal you hope to achieve in the next few years.
points: what you are doing to achieve it
cards.explain: and explain how you will feel when you achieve it.
followUp: Is it important to set goals?
Why do many people give up on their goals?
Should schools teach students how to plan their future?
Is it important to plan your life carefully?
Do you think success depends more on hard work or on luck?

cards.title: Describe a film that made you think.
cards.explain: and explain why it made you think.
followUp: Can films change people's opinions?
Are cinemas still popular in your country?
Should films based on true stories stay close to the facts?
Should films be used in schools to teach? Why?
Will cinemas still exist in twenty years?

cards.title: Describe a time you helped someone.
cards.explain: and explain how you felt afterwards.
followUp: Why do some people volunteer?
Should helping in the community be part of school?
Are people less helpful in big cities?
Should helping others be taught at school?
Why do some people volunteer without being paid?

cards.title: Describe a building you find interesting.
cards.explain: and explain why you find it interesting.
followUp: Should old buildings be protected or replaced?
What makes a city attractive?
How will buildings change in the future?
Should old buildings be protected or replaced with modern ones?
Who should decide what new buildings look like?

cards.title: Describe a teacher who influenced you.
cards.explain: and explain how they influenced you.
followUp: What makes a good teacher?
Should teachers be paid more than they are now?
Will online learning replace teachers?
Is it better to study alone or in a group?
How has education changed since your parents were at school?

cards.title: Describe an online course or video that taught you something.
cards.explain: and explain whether you would recommend it to others.
followUp: What are the advantages of studying online?
Why do many people not finish online courses?
Should universities offer all their courses online?
Can you learn practical skills from videos?
How can people stay motivated when they study alone?

cards.title: Describe an app on your phone that you find useful.
cards.explain: and explain why it is useful to you.
followUp: Do people spend too much time on their phones?
Should children have smartphones?
How do apps collect money if they are free?
What jobs might disappear because of technology?
Is social media good for friendships?

cards.title: Describe an invention that has changed the way people live.
cards.explain: and explain how it has changed people's lives.
followUp: Which invention of the last century is the most important?
Do all inventions make life better?
Should governments pay for scientific research?
Why do some people resist new technology?
What will be the next big invention?

cards.title: Describe a friend you have known for a long time.
cards.explain: and explain why your friendship has lasted.
followUp: What makes a good friend?
Is it easy to make friends as an adult?
Can you be real friends with someone online?
Are friends more important than family?
Why do friendships sometimes end?

cards.title: Describe a neighbour you know well.
points: how long you have known them
cards.explain: and explain why you get on well with them.
followUp: Do people know their neighbours less than in the past?
How can neighbours help each other?
Is it better to live in a house or a flat?
What problems can happen between neighbours?
Should cities create more community spaces?

cards.title: Describe a city you would like to visit.
cards.explain: and explain why you would like to visit it.
followUp: What makes a city a good place to live?
Is tourism good for cities?
Should old city centres be closed to cars?
Why do people move from the countryside to cities?
How will cities change in the future?

cards.title: Describe a park or garden you enjoy visiting.
cards.explain: and explain why you enjoy going there.
followUp: Why are green spaces important in cities?
Should people grow their own food?
Do children spend enough time outdoors?
Who should pay for public parks?
How can cities be made greener?

cards.title: Describe a time when the weather changed your plans.
cards.explain: and explain what you did instead.
followUp: How is the climate changing in your country?
What can individuals do to protect the environment?
Should governments or companies do more about pollution?
Do people take weather forecasts seriously?
How does weather affect people's moods?

cards.title: Describe a healthy habit you have.
cards.explain: and explain how it helps you.
followUp: Why is it hard for people to change their habits?
Should junk food be taxed?
Is it the government's job to keep people healthy?
Do people worry too much about their health today?
How can schools help children to eat well?

cards.title: Describe a job you would like to do in the future.
cards.explain: and explain why you would like to do it.
followUp: What is more important in a job: money or satisfaction?
Should people stay in one job for many years?
Is working from home a good idea?
Which jobs will be most important in the future?
Should students work while they study?

cards.title: Describe a tradition in your country that you like.
cards.explain: and explain why you like it.
followUp: Why do some traditions disappear?
Should young people learn about old traditions?
Is globalisation making cultures more similar?
How do festivals help tourism?
Can new traditions be created?
